heading: Suspect killed in ‘encounter’ amid cross-border claims of ASI killing plot
author: Kamaldeep Singh Brar
paragraphs: The Punjab Police claimed that an accused in the killing of Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Harjeet Singh was neutralised during a late-night encounter in Amritsar on the intervening night of Saturday and Sunday.

Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill said police have identified the suspect as a 20-year-old Deepak Singh of Mule Chak village. Deepak was traveling on a scooter with an accomplice when officers signaled them to stop at a checkpoint on Thande Road, the officer said.
Police alleged that the suspects fled, prompting a chase, and then allegedly opened fire by discharging four rounds at the police team.

Two bullets reportedly hit the police vehicle, and one struck a Counter Intelligence officer’s bulletproof jacket, police alleged. Officers also said they fired six rounds in self-defense, hitting Deepak, who died en route to the hospital, while his associate escaped.
Police said the handlers in Pakistan had directed the attack on the ASI on the night of September 18 in the Dana Mandi area.

Deepak’s family claimed that he worked as a labourer installing telecom towers, but he rarely stayed at home and spent most of his time outside. They also alleged that in September he was falsely accused of possessing 500 grams of contraband and was booked under an NDPS Act case.

Addressing the police claims regarding his alleged cross-border ties, his parents maintained that Deepak never mentioned any contact with handlers in Pakistan or receiving instructions to target police officers. They also said they did not know any associates he kept.

Before the encounter, Deepak had been missing from home for three to four days. His parents had actively searched for him at the Makboolpura Gate police station and intended to present him to the authorities alongside the village Sarpanch, once located.
They ultimately learned of his death in the police encounter through local television broadcasts.
